newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Dubai active prior to India's tender.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Dubai active prior to India's tender.

text.p: Asia's heavy crude prices were steady with sellers holding back, unwilling to offer lower levels despite thinner Japanese buying, traders said on Wednesday.
But Minas remained supported by tighter August supplies.
A 300,000 barrel cargo of August Minas was sold by a shosha to an Indonesian affiliate at ICP +75 cents per barrel.
Limited activity was seen for other heavy Indonesian grades as sellers wait for firm buyers to emerge.
The September market remained dominated by Dubai trades, as buyers cover their position before the close of India's buy tender on Thursday.
A shosha bought a September Dubai cargo at whole month quotes -12 cents from a Malaysian trading company.
The seller was heard to have subsequently boought a Dubai cargo from a European major at whole month quotes -15 cents.
But this trade could not be confirmed.
Another Dubai cargo was traded at whole month quotes -15, although this was heard to be a cargo that a Japanese refiner had sold back to its term supplier, a European major.
Traders said that the refiner preferred lighter crudes for September for winter stockpiling, prompting the sale of the cargo.
August Masila was confirmed sold to Thailand, although the trade was done a week ago.
Thailand denied rumours that the trade was done at Dubai -15, saying that the trade was on an OSP related level.
